task.title: Deactivate selected tools atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/633 by revoking an exact selected tool batch without filesystem access, guest execution, or partial registry mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight duplicate and missing exact IDs before removing any registered adapter.
Reject non-tool selection records before registry mutation.
Remove only the complete selected batch while preserving unrelated adapters.
Treat empty deactivation as a process-local no-op and require revalidation for later reactivation.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for atomic batch revocation.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused tests could not compile because ToolRegistryRemovalError, ToolRegistry::unregister_all, and deactivate_tool_selection did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added kernel and extension tests for exact removal, deterministic duplicate and missing diagnostics, wrong-kind rejection, empty success, and unchanged registry state on failure.

attempts.diagnostic: Validating the complete exact-ID set before mutation allows selected adapters to be revoked without rebuilding or touching unrelated adapters.
attempts.patch: Added the typed kernel batch-removal primitive, the selected-tool extension boundary, source-preserving error mapping, docs, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Corrected lifecycle documentation after substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: The first documentation update still listed registry removal as a non-goal even though the change introduced atomic removal.
attempts.patch: Removed the stale removal non-goal, reran verification, and resolved the review thread on the exact replacement commit.

outcome.summary: Callers can now atomically revoke exact selected process-local tool adapters while failures preserve the complete registry and later reactivation must repeat the existing safe activation boundary.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test tool_registry
nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-extensions --test activation

GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30220902288 and resolved substantive CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/634#discussion_r3653452682

lessons: Revocation should validate the whole exact-ID batch before dropping any adapter.
Capability kind remains part of lifecycle authority even when an unrelated adapter has the same ID.
Deactivation needs no filesystem lease, but reactivation must reacquire and revalidate artifacts.
Lifecycle documentation should be checked for stale non-goals whenever a previously unsupported operation is added.
